new_statements.quote: В языке бага форе два уровневых тона: высокий (á) и низкий (à).
new_statements.translation: The Baga Fore language has two level tones: high (á) and low (à).
new_statements.citation: Golovko, E. V. 2015. Imennye klassy v jazyke baga fore: predvaritel'nye dannye. In: V. A. Vinogradov (otv. red.), A. I. Koval', A. B. Shluinskij (eds.), Issledovanija po jazykam Afriki, vyp. 5, 55-68. Moskva: Ključ-S.
new_statements.locator: Section 1 'Некоторые сведения о бага форе', p. 55 (sentence immediately below Table 2, consonant phonemes)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (342 pp., text, PDF page = printed page). Golovko's article 'Именные классы в языке бага форе: предварительные данные' occupies pp. 54-68 (title page 54 is unnumbered; the compiler '55-68' is off by one, Glottolog's 54-68 is right; volume redkollegija is V. A. Vinogradov (otv. red.), A. I. Koval', A. B. Shluinskij as the compiler says, not Vydrin). Section 1 'Некоторые сведения о бага форе' (pp. 54-55) gives 7 vowel phonemes (Table 1), the consonant table (Table 2), and directly beneath Table 2 on p. 55 the sentence 'В языке бага форе два уровневых тона: высокий (á) и низкий (à).' — verbatim as quoted. I extracted pp. 54-68 and a full-text search for stress/accent удар-/акцент-/просо…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only published first-hand prosodic statement: Baga Fore (Mbulungish) is described as a tone language with two level tones (H, L), marked on the author's transcriptions (e.g. cí-wɔ̀nàn 'shadow', Ø-bàrtɛ́ 'lion'). Nothing is said about word stress or accent; no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author flags all data as preliminary (first fieldwork Dec 2013 - Jan 2014, 'первые собранные материалы.. будут уточнены и проверены').
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical tone on words in citation form; no discussion of phrase-level prosody. Rochant 2023 (p. 229 fn. 79) confirms second-hand that no published account of the Mbulungish tonal system exists.
new_statements.identity_note: Golovko 2015 describes 'baga fore' (бага форе) as spoken around the village of Monchon (Моншон), sous-préfecture Boffa, Guinea — this is Glottolog mbul1258 Mbulungish (alt. names Baga Foré, Monchon, Black Baga); Rochant 2023 calls the same language 'Baga Mbulungish (aka Baga Fore)'. No dialect split is described.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: On the sister language Pukur (Baga Mboteni), not Mbulungish. Second-hand for Mbulungish: 'all the three languages of the hypothetical Nalu branch feature tone (for Baga Mbulungish, see GOLOVKO 2015: 55..)' and p. 229 fn. 79: 'Nalu and Baga Mbulungish.. are reported to have tone by SEIDEL (2013a) and GOLOVKO (2015). However, there are no published materials available on their tonal systems'. States (p. 22) that research on Baga Mbulungish 'is confined to a single published paper' (Golovko 2015) plus unpublished Golovko data; lists Wilson 2007 as containing short wordlists and brief grammatical…
No phonology content; references Fields-Black 2008, Wilson 2007, Sapir 1971, Pozdniakov BRE entries.
